entry.title: [AutoMapper] AutoMapper: Uncontrolled Recursion with Constructor Parameters
entry.content:
Summary

MaxDepth, whether set explicitly or applied by default (64) to self-referential type maps, was not enforced when the recursion goes through constructor parameters. Mapping a deeply nested source to a destination built through its constructor, such as a positional record, recurses without bound and throws a StackOverflowException. That exception can't be caught and terminates the process. This bypasses the mitigation for CVE-2026-32933.

Details

The type depth used by MaxDepth was incremented only after the destination object was created. Constructor parameters, including child objects of the same type, are mapped while the destination is created, so each level recursed before its parent was counted, and the depth check never tripped.

Affected:

  • destination types mapped through constructor parameters, including positional records
  • both an explicit MaxDepth(n) and the default limit of 64
  • ConstructUsing that maps recursively through context.Mapper

With MaxDepth(10), a 100-level chain was mapped to all 100 levels. On a 1 MB stack (the Windows default), the process crashed at between 1,000 and 2,000 levels.

PoC

The type only has a constructor with positional arguments, and MaxDepth is set to 10:

using AutoMapper;


// Setup configuration - with MaxDepth set
var mapper = new MapperConfiguration(cfg =>
    {
        cfg.CreateMap<CircularClass, CircularClass>().MaxDepth(10);
    })
    .CreateMapper();

// Create a deeply nested object (28,000+ levels)
var root = new CircularClass(null);
var current = root;
for (int i = 0; i < 30000; i++)
{
    current.Next = new CircularClass(null);
    current = current.Next;
}

// STACK OVERFLOW even though the max depth is set
var mappedRoot = mapper.Map<CircularClass>(root);


public class CircularClass
{
    public CircularClass(CircularClass? Next)
    {
        this.Next = Next;
    }

    public CircularClass? Next { get; set; }
}

Impact

Any application that maps attacker-influenced, deeply nested data to a destination type built through a constructor, with a recursive member, can be crashed. Setting MaxDepth as recommended for CVE-2026-32933 doesn't protect these mappings.

Patches

Fixed in 16.3.0 and 15.1.4. The depth is now counted before the destination is created, so constructor mapping stops at the same depth as property mapping.

Workarounds

If the destination type has a parameterless constructor and settable properties, cfg.DisableConstructorMapping() makes AutoMapper map through the properties, where MaxDepth is enforced. Positional records have no workaround other than limiting input depth before mapping, or upgrading.

Credits

Reported by @mcambria, who found it while writing a test to confirm their MaxDepth mitigation for CVE-2026-32933.

Related

  • CVE-2026-32933 (GHSA-rvv3-g6hj-g44x)
  • GHSA-gpwp-5797-mjff: other paths that bypassed MaxDepth (polymorphic maps, runtime-typed members, dictionary and dynamic sources, recursive type converters), fixed in the same releases.

entry.title: [AutoMapper] AutoMapper: Denial of Service via uncontrolled recursion that bypasses MaxDepth
entry.content:
Summary

The default and explicit MaxDepth limits added for CVE-2026-32933 don't apply to several mapping paths. Mapping a deeply nested source through any of them recurses without bound and throws a StackOverflowException, which can't be caught and terminates the process.

Affected paths

  • Polymorphic maps: derived type maps (Include / IncludeBase) didn't inherit the base map's MaxDepth, and the default limit for self-referential maps was only applied to the base map. A chain of derived objects was mapped without a limit, even with MaxDepth set on the base map.
  • Runtime-typed members: members typed as object or an interface aren't seen by self-reference detection, so the default limit isn't applied.
  • Dictionary and dynamic sources: mapping a nested Dictionary<string, object> or ExpandoObject (for example, deserialized JSON) onto typed destinations recurses with no depth tracking. MaxDepth has no effect.
  • Recursive type converters: ConvertUsing that calls context.Mapper.Map ignores MaxDepth.

Impact

An application that maps attacker-influenced, deeply nested data through one of these paths can be crashed. On a 1 MB stack (the Windows default), a few thousand levels of nesting are enough.

Fix

  • Derived type maps inherit MaxDepth, and the default limit is applied to them.
  • Every runtime map call checks for sufficient stack, and fails with a catchable InsufficientExecutionStackException instead of overflowing.

Workarounds

Set MaxDepth explicitly on derived maps and on maps reached through object or interface members. There is no configuration workaround for dictionary or dynamic sources, or for recursive type converters, other than limiting input depth before mapping.

Related

  • CVE-2026-32933 (GHSA-rvv3-g6hj-g44x)
  • GHSA-6vhm-j9h7-f9gh: MaxDepth not enforced through constructor parameters and positional records, fixed in the same releases.

entry.title: [Aspire.Dashboard.Sdk.win-arm64] Microsoft Security Advisory CVE-2026-118740 - Aspire Security Feature Bypass Vulnerability
entry.content:
Executive summary

Microsoft is releasing this security advisory to provide information about a vulnerability in Aspire. This advisory provides guidance on updating affected applications and components.

Aspire Dashboard's unauthenticated NotFound route can permit telemetry deletion in both standalone and AppHost-hosted deployments. In standalone deployments using browser-token authentication, it can also expose the browser token.

Announcement

Announcement for this issue can be found at https://github.com/dotnet/announcements/issues/526

CVSS Details

  • Version: 3.1
  • Severity: Critical
  • Score: 9.1
  • Vector: CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:N
  • Weakness: CWE-862

Affected Platforms

  • Platforms: Any supported OS
  • Architectures: x64, Arm64

Affected Packages

Standalone Aspire Dashboard

Package Affected version Patched version
Aspire Dashboard < 13.6.5 13.6.5

Both 13.6.3 and 13.6.4 contain the unauthenticated NotFound route.

Aspire Dashboard SDK packages

Package Affected version Patched version
Aspire.Dashboard.Sdk.linux-x64 < 13.6.5 13.6.5
Aspire.Dashboard.Sdk.linux-arm64 < 13.6.5 13.6.5
Aspire.Dashboard.Sdk.linux-musl-x64 < 13.6.5 13.6.5
Aspire.Dashboard.Sdk.osx-x64 < 13.6.5 13.6.5
Aspire.Dashboard.Sdk.osx-arm64 < 13.6.5 13.6.5
Aspire.Dashboard.Sdk.win-x64 < 13.6.5 13.6.5
Aspire.Dashboard.Sdk.win-arm64 < 13.6.5 13.6.5

Advisory FAQ

How do I know if I am affected?

Aspire Dashboard releases through 13.6.4 are affected, whether deployed independently or launched by an Aspire AppHost. For an AppHost using Dashboard SDK packages, check the resolved Aspire.Dashboard.Sdk package versions against the affected ranges above. If the AppHost selects a CLI-bundled Dashboard or a custom Dashboard path, check the version of that Dashboard instead. Aspire ships independently of .NET; installing a .NET runtime or SDK update does not replace the Dashboard.

How do I fix the issue?

Update Aspire Dashboard to version 13.6.5 or later. Neither 13.6.3 nor 13.6.4 is a fixed upgrade target.

For container deployments, explicitly set the Dashboard image to mcr.microsoft.com/aspire/dashboard:13.6.5 and recreate or redeploy the container. Replace older version tags and nightly image references, including those in generated Docker Compose or Kubernetes manifests, with this fixed stable image. Updating AppHost package references alone does not replace an image reference in an existing deployment manifest.

For an AppHost using Dashboard SDK packages, update any explicit Aspire.Hosting.AppHost version, including a central package version, to 13.6.5 or later. If that reference is supplied implicitly by Aspire.AppHost.Sdk, update the SDK reference to 13.6.5 or later instead. Restore and rebuild the AppHost, verify that its resolved Aspire.Dashboard.Sdk packages are 13.6.5 or later, and restart the AppHost to run the updated Dashboard.

If your AppHost selects a CLI-bundled Dashboard or a custom Dashboard path, update the Dashboard in that selected bundle or location to 13.6.5 or later and restart the AppHost. Updating AppHost package references alone does not replace that Dashboard.

Other Information

Reporting Security Issues

If you have found a potential security issue in a supported version of .NET, please report it to the Microsoft Security Response Center (MSRC) via the MSRC Researcher Portal. Further information can be found in the MSRC Report an Issue FAQ.

Security reports made through MSRC may qualify for the Microsoft .NET Bounty. Details of the Microsoft .NET Bounty Program including terms and conditions are at https://aka.ms/corebounty.

Support

You can ask questions about this issue in the Aspire repository at https://github.com/microsoft/aspire. The Announcements repo (https://github.com/dotnet/Announcements) will contain this bulletin as an issue and will include a link to a discussion issue. You can ask questions in the linked discussion issue.
